ArrayMesh Circular Array (12 columns around a colonnade)

Look at `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj`. It contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Column, is an axis-aligned cuboid of size 0.2 x 2.0 x 0.2 BU (width x height x depth) centred at world position (-2, 1, 0). The column therefore extends x in [-2.1, -1.9], y in [0, 2], z in [-0.1, 0.1]. The mesh has 8 vertices and 6 quad faces, a single default polygroup, no UVs, and no polypaint.

Load this OBJ into ZBrush and use ArrayMesh to create a circular array of 12 copies of the column, equally spaced 30 degrees apart around the world Y axis, so that each copy's centroid lies on a circle of radius 2.0 BU in the XZ plane at height y = 1. Bake the array into real geometry, produce 12 individual SubTools named Col_01 through Col_12, and export the result as `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj`.

The exported `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy:

- Exactly 12 SubTools, named Col_01 through Col_12.
- Each SubTool has exactly 8 vertices and 6 quad faces.
- Each SubTool's centroid projected onto the XZ plane lies on a circle of radius 2.0 BU within 0.02 BU.
- Each SubTool's Y extent is [0, 2] within 0.01 BU.
- Consecutive columns' centroid angles, sorted around the Y axis, differ by 30 degrees within 0.5 degree.
